format_learned.keys: id, area (m2, float; listing area, appears converted from sqft), net_area (unreliable: 0 in ~32% of plans, >area in ~11%), wall_depth (canvas units), inner, land, neighbor (tuple), wall, door, window, front_door, living, bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, balcony, storage, stair, garden, parking, pool (shapely Polygon/MultiPolygon); area_change_sqft only on 683 augmented plans
format_learned.coordinates: Canvas units, NOT metres: every plan is normalised so its 'inner' footprint spans 256 units on its longer side. README's 'metric-scale coordinates' is realised via the per-plan 'area' field.
format_learned.room_taxonomy: living (living+dining+hall+corridors merged, one label), bedroom, bathroom (no separate WC label), kitchen, balcony, storage, stair; plus non-room layers garden/parking/pool/land/neighbor. No dining, corridor, laundry, maid, majlis labels.

method.plans_used: Original plans only: the 683 augmented plans (key area_change_sqft; rotations/flips/rescales of 667 originals) are excluded. Near-duplicate listings (~6.9% per README) could not be removed (dedup list not in the downloaded file).
method.metric_calibration: Per plan: metres_per_unit s = sqrt(area_m2 / inner.area_units). Checks: resulting wall thickness median 0.22 m (typical 9-inch brick 0.229 m), 99.5% within 0.10-0.40 m (README reports 99.3%); room polygons sum to ~96.5% of 'inner'.
method.calibration_uncertainty: Door openings under this scale: bedroom 1.04 m, bathroom 0.96 m, front 1.21 m (medians) - roughly 10-15% wider than South Asian leaf+frame norms, and where net_area is plausible (0.5-0.95 x area, 47% of plans) its median ratio to area is 0.723, typical of carpet vs super-built-up area. So listing 'area' may often be a built-up/super-built-up figure. If so, multiply the lengths here by ~0.85 and the areas by ~0.72 (lower bound). The validator should treat room-size percentiles as +/-15% (linear) uncertain; shares, counts, ratios and adjacency frequencies are scale-free and unaffected.
method.qc_exclusions: listed area < 20 m2; wall thickness outside 0.08-0.50 m after scaling; room parts < 0.5 m2 dropped as vectorisation crumbs.
method.room_metrics: area = polygon area (net, inside walls); short/long side = minimum rotated rectangle; inscribed_width = diameter of maximum inscribed circle (usable clear width for L-shapes); aspect = long/short of MRR; rectangular = area/MRR area >= 0.95.
method.living: All 'living' parts of a plan are unioned into one living_zone node (resplan_utils convention). It therefore includes dining, entrance hall, lobby and corridors.
method.doors: Each door polygon is assigned to the <=2 rooms it touches (buffer 0.007 x 256 units ~0.1 m), ties broken by contact length as in resplan_utils.plan_to_graph. doors_per_room counts interior door polygons only; front door reported separately (has_front_door_share).
method.connections: door = shared door polygon; open = wall-free passage >= 2 wall thicknesses wide (resplan_utils via_opening logic, with doors/windows also treated as obstacles); interior_window_passthrough = window polygon shared by two interior rooms (resplan_utils promotes these to via_door; 9.1k plans have one between kitchen and living, i.e. a counter/pass-through or semi-open kitchen); access = door OR open OR interior_window_passthrough; window_only = window shared with a balcony (not walkable); adjacent = shares >= 0.5 m of boundary within 1.3 wall thickness, or connected.
method.pair_plan_share: For type pair A|B: among plans containing both (for A|A: >= 2 rooms of A), the share with >= 1 connection of each kind.
method.access_to_share: Per room of the given kind: share of such rooms having >= 1 connection of that kind to a room of the target type.
method.circulation: No corridor label exists. living_zone_share_of_net_interior is an UPPER bound (living+dining+hall+corridor). corridor_like_share = (parts of the living zone narrower than 1.5 m [or 1.8 m], pieces >= 1 m2 and >= 0.7 m wide, found by morphological opening + stair area) / net interior area - a LOWER-bound heuristic for dedicated corridors.
method.bathroom_roles: ensuite = accessible from a bedroom and not from living/kitchen; shared = from a bedroom and from living/kitchen; common = not from any bedroom. master = largest bedroom in plans with >= 2 bedrooms.
method.segments: all = every QC-passed original plan; bed4plus = >= 4 bedrooms (the villa comparator); bed3 = exactly 3 bedrooms; house_like = plan has garden or parking or stair layer (closest thing to a detached house in ResPlan); bed4plus_house_like if >= 50 plans.

majlis.quality: none - no majlis label; South Asian drawing room is merged into 'living'

family_living.quality: poor - living label also contains dining, hall, corridors

kitchen.quality: good (one kitchen per plan; ~78% of kitchens are open or pass-through to living, ~22% have a door)

guest_wc.quality: fair - no WC label; small common bathrooms are the analogue

maid_room.quality: poor - no staff-room label; in >=4-bed plans ~9% of 'bedrooms' are < 8 m2 and ~32% of kitchens connect to a bedroom, consistent with a servant room off the kitchen

balcony_terrace.quality: good for balconies; no roof terraces

caveats: Apartments, not villas: ResPlan is single-floor unit plans from South Asian real-estate listings (README 'Known limitations'); median listed area ~110 m2 vs a Gulf 4-bed villa of 350-600 m2. Use as typicality warnings only, never as hard rules.

Regional bias: South Asian layout conventions (open kitchens, balcony-heavy, compact bedrooms, many attached baths). Not representative of Gulf villas (majlis, separate dining, maid/driver quarters, dirty kitchen).
Only 7 room labels: living merges living/dining/hall/corridor; no WC, laundry, maid, majlis, dining, corridor labels, so several villa roles have no direct comparator (see villa_role_map).

Metric scale is derived from the listing's area field; evidence suggests it is often a built-up figure, so lengths may be overstated by up to ~15% and areas by up to ~28% (see method.calibration_uncertainty).
>=4-bedroom plans are a small subset (~6% of plans) and are still apartments, mostly single-level.
Near-duplicate listings (~6.9%) are not removed; percentiles are barely affected but counts are not fully independent.
Door/opening/adjacency detection is geometric and inherits vectorisation artefacts (jagged contours, windows drawn on kitchen-living boundaries).
Licence discrepancy: repo LICENSE says CC BY 4.0 for the data, but croissant.json says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Attribution is required either way.
